key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation follows different solid-state conversion pathways in wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap perovskite stacks, so bandgap control must be tailored to the specific absorber chemistry.
engineering_relevance: This work enables solvent-free fabrication of all-perovskite tandem solar cells with tunable bandgaps and a demonstrated 19.2% power conversion efficiency.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Comparison of mixed-halide WBG and Sn-Pb NBG solid-state conversion
Guided absorber design based on conversion behavior and composition gradients
evidence_signal: The paper reports sTE absorbers spanning 1.26-1.96 eV, a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem at 19.2% efficiency, and 80% average efficiency retention after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: Absolute thickness control and vertical compositional gradients are critical, so small deviations in evaporated precursor layering or annealing could strongly affect the final bandgap and device performance.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
